frameworks.name: Three Types of Debt
frameworks.definition: A classification of debt including financial debt, ignorance debt (knowledge and skills), and the cost of not learning.

frameworks.name: Expert Definition Through Mistakes
frameworks.definition: An expert is someone who has made all the mistakes possible in a narrow field; expertise is built by learning to lose first.

claims.text: Ignorance debt is the biggest and most expensive debt. It's the cost of what you do not know but should know (Alex Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: You have to learn how to lose before you can learn how to win. If you don't fail, you will never acquire the knowledge you need (Alex Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Failure is the experiential path to knowledge acquisition; without failure, knowledge remains unprocessed.

claims.text: An expert is just somebody who's made all the mistakes you can make in a very narrow field (Alex Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: Does not apply to domains where mistakes carry existential risk or irreversible harm

claims.text: The first rule of losing is that you didn't lose, you just learned. You paid down the most expensive debt (Alex Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: I am willing to pay in looking bad, in money lost, in time lost, in people judging me to make bets and gain knowledge (Alex Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Knowledge acquisition required for business growth

claims.text: I still pay off ignorance debt every day. It's the debt in skills and knowledge that I should know to get faster and further to where I'm trying to go, but I don't (Alex Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: If you know that you have to pay off ignorance debt, why aren't you? It's because you don't realize how expensive not paying it off really is (Alex Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Underestimating the cost of ignored ignorance debt creates psychological permission to defer learning investments.

examples.text: Hormozi's Acquisition.com portfolio analyzed 10 stages of growth across portfolio companies. They identified where companies got stuck and how they got past it, then created a 10-stage quiz to help business owners identify their current stage and prioritize function-specific work (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, finance).

practices.text: Take purposeful action despite fear or discomfort in order to gain knowledge, because confidence is a retroactive result of action, not a precondition.
Identify the growth stage your business is in using a structured roadmap, then focus on the most important function-specific work to deconstraint each business lever.
